newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar up despite increase in free sale quota.
newsitem.headline: India sugar up despite increase in free sale quota.

text.p: Indian sugar prices extended gains on Friday despite the release of additional free sale quota for the current month, dealers said.
Continued buying by large consumers for the summer season and a shortage of stock helped prices to move up, they said.

"The Indian government released an additional free sale quota of 50,000 tonnes for the current month but this has failed to arrest rising prices as demand remians higher higher then supply," one trader said.
"Actually traders had earlier expected that government may release an additional quota of at least 100,000 tonnes but as it was less, prices quickly bounced back," he said.
The government hiked free sale quota for May by 50,000 tonnes to 800,000 tonnes.
In ready delivery, sugar S-30 rose 10 rupees to 1,400/1,450 rupees per quintal and M-30 moved up 20 rupees to 1,460/1,505 rupees per quintal, dealers said.
Sugar mill delivery moved up 10 rupees to 1,350/1,370 rupees per quintal on higher buying by mills, traders said.
They said higher purchases by mills in neighbouring states reduced supply in the Bombay market.
